stories.headline: Kremlin critic says Ukraine war ‘backfiring’ on Putin as discontent grows
stories.summary: Vladimir Kara-Murza, a Russian opposition politician, stated that the war in Ukraine is "backfiring" on President Vladimir Putin's regime. Mounting military and economic failures have eroded Putin's strongman image, exposing him as increasingly vulnerable. The war has led to a stalemate in Ukraine and growing war fatigue among Russians. Ukrainian drone strikes against Russian forces and inside Russian territory have fueled criticism of Putin. As a result, discontent is growing, stripping away Putin's strongman image. The Kremlin's struggles have created an opportunity for critics like Kara-Murza to speak out against the regime. Putin is facing challenges in changing the narrative of the war, which has led to increased scrutiny of his leadership. The situation continues to unfold, with Kara-Murza's comments highlighting the regime's vulnerabilities.

stories.headline: Russia warns war costs are ravaging its finances as Ukrainian 'drone overmatch' halts Putin's forces
stories.summary: Russia's finance ministry has warned of deteriorating finances due to the ongoing war with Ukraine, estimating a potential overspend of ₽2trn. The ministry has urged the cabinet to freeze around ₽2.9 trillion in non-war-related spending to mitigate the issue. The war is consuming 40% of Russia's budget, and sanctions, as well as Ukrainian drones, are impacting oil revenues. Ukrainian forces have achieved "temporary tactical drone overmatch" in some sectors, slowing Russian operations. The Russian government has instructed top banks to handle the costs of defending against Ukrainian drones and to shoot them down themselves. The financial strain, combined with a manpower crisis and collapsing birth rate, is taking a significant toll on Russia's economy and war efforts, with no clear solution in sight to address these interconnected challenges. The war's costs are now severely impacting Russia's finances.

stories.headline: Kenya Arrests 8 Students After Fire at School Dorm Kills 16
stories.summary: A fire at Utumishi Girls Academy in Gilgil, Kenya, killed 16 students and injured 79 others. The blaze broke out in a crowded dormitory, exposing safety lapses. Kenyan police arrested eight female students suspected of launching the fatal arson attack. The students are being held in connection with the incident, which occurred at the police-run girls' boarding school. The fire resulted in significant loss of life and injuries, with at least 79 students hospitalized. The arrests were made as part of an investigation into the cause of the fire and the circumstances surrounding the incident. The school and authorities are facing questions about safety measures and how the fire was able to spread so quickly.

stories.headline: Trump claims to be on verge of approving peace deal with major Iranian concessions
stories.summary: President Donald Trump claims to be on the verge of approving a peace deal with Iran, containing major concessions from Tehran. The deal reportedly includes the opening of the Strait of Hormuz without tolls and Iran agreeing to never have a nuclear weapon. Trump stated that Iran must reopen the Strait immediately. Additionally, Trump said Iran has agreed to hand over its enriched uranium. The US and Iranian negotiators have reportedly come to terms on a tentative agreement, following high-level White House talks. Trump indicated that Washington and Tehran were "very close" to a peace deal, with an announcement potentially made on Friday. The development comes after several news outlets reported on the progress of the negotiations between the two countries.

stories.headline: [Game Informer] Call Of Duty: Warzone For PS4 And Xbox One Is Being Delisted And Will Shut Down Later This Year
stories.summary: Call of Duty: Warzone for PlayStation 4 and Xbox One is being delisted and will shut down later this year. The game's in-game store will be removed from PS4 and Xbox One on June 25, although players can still redeem COD Points until this date. After June 25, the store will no longer be accessible on these platforms. The delisting is part of Activision's plan to focus on current-generation consoles. Call of Duty: Warzone Caldera will also be shutting down later this year, with only the current Warzone version available after. Players on last-gen consoles can continue playing until the shutdown, but with limited functionality after the in-game store removal. The exact shutdown date for Warzone on PS4 and Xbox One has not been announced.

stories.headline: [Notebookcheck] Nintendo Support addresses Switch 2 HDMI cables missing from console's box
stories.summary: Nintendo Support has acknowledged an issue with the Switch 2 console, where some boxes are missing the included HDMI cable for the dock. This has caused inconvenience for gamers who expect the cable to be part of the package. The problem is the latest in a series of issues reported with the Switch 2 dock, including faulty Ethernet ports. Nintendo Support has confirmed that the missing HDMI cable is a known issue and is likely to be addressed. The Switch 2 has been experiencing other technical issues, such as problems with HDMI cords, with some users reporting that the console is damaging the cables. The issue with the missing HDMI cable comes after Nintendo announced a price increase for the Switch 2 in its 2026 fiscal report.

stories.headline: [the-decoder.com] Google fixes several bugs in Gemini usage limits that burned through quotas too fast
stories.summary: Google has fixed several bugs in Gemini's usage limits that were causing quotas to be burned through too quickly. A bug was causing one or two Omni videos to use up the entire quota, but this has been resolved. Ultra members now receive double the number of Omni video generations. Additionally, Google is capping the quota usage for single prompts and making Flash-Lite prompts free. Failed AI requests will no longer count against user quotas, and usage will only be charged for successful completions. The updates also include a detailed usage breakdown and notification features on the usage limit page, allowing users to utilize the Gemini app more efficiently. These changes aim to address user complaints about unexpectedly high quota consumption and provide a fairer usage experience.

stories.headline: [MakeUseOf] This app might be the best thing about owning a Samsung phone Good Lock is the app that unlocks your Galaxy phone's hidden functionality
stories.summary: Samsung's Good Lock app unlocks hidden functionality in Galaxy phones, offering a powerful customization suite. The app provides a collection of modules and plugins that allow users to personalize almost every aspect of their device. With Good Lock, users can customize their interface, enhance productivity, and improve overall functionality. The app has been updated with new features, including code for unreleased functions such as video softening and autofocus speed. Good Lock is exclusive to Samsung Galaxy devices, making it a unique benefit for owners of these phones. The app's customization capabilities have been praised by users, who appreciate the ability to fully personalize their device. By utilizing Good Lock, Samsung Galaxy phone owners can unlock new possibilities and enhance their overall user experience.

stories.headline: [Daily Express] Transfer news LIVE: Konate to Chelsea, Man Utd confirm £31m deal
stories.summary: Manchester United has confirmed a £31m deal, while Arsenal is set to exit with a £45m transfer. Meanwhile, Chelsea is reportedly close to signing Ibrahima Konate, with the defender's Liverpool contract extension talks seemingly stalled. In a separate deal, Chelsea has agreed to sign goalkeeper Filip Jørgensen from Villarreal for a €24.5m fee, with the player set to sign a long-term contract. The transfer market continues to see significant activity, with various clubs negotiating deals and exits. Manchester United is also reportedly close to agreeing on a £26m deal, despite initial difficulties in negotiations. These developments highlight the ongoing transfer activity in the football world.

stories.headline: [SPORTbible] Arsenal enter race for unthinkable Premier League transfer as Real Madrid and Man City circle
stories.summary: Arsenal have joined the race for a world-class midfielder from a Premier League rival, facing competition from Manchester City and Real Madrid. The midfielder's current deal expires in 2029, and several top clubs, including PSG and Bayern Munich, are monitoring his situation. Meanwhile, Barcelona are plotting a move for Arsenal defender Piero Hincapie, who helped the Gunners win the Premier League title and reach the Champions League final. Arsenal are also among the suitors for 16-year-old Leicester attacker Monga, who is expected to leave the Foxes after their relegation. The Gunners are competing with Manchester United and Manchester City for Monga's signature. Arsenal are currently top of the Premier League, nine points clear of nearest challengers Manchester City, and are preparing for a potential summer transfer splurge, monitoring several players from the same Premier League club.

stories.headline: [Goal.com] Folarin Balogun with the ‘big boys’ & Ricardo Pepi at ‘mid to lower team’ - USMNT strikers the subject of Premier League transfer predictions
stories.summary: USMNT strikers Folarin Balogun and Ricardo Pepi are subjects of Premier League transfer predictions. Former goalkeeper Brad Friedel believes both players could end up in the English top-flight. Friedel suggests that Balogun, considered one of the "big boys," may join a top-tier team, while Pepi would be a better fit for a mid to lower-tier team, such as Brentford, Bournemouth, or Fulham. These teams have lower expectations and pressure, which could benefit Pepi's development. The predictions come as the summer transfer window approaches, with both players potentially making moves to enhance their careers. The USMNT strikers have shown promise, with Balogun and Pepi being considered for the World Cup roster alongside other potent goal-scorers. Their potential transfers are being closely watched in the football world.

stories.headline: [Barca Blaugranes] The five biggest dream matches at the 2026 World Cup
stories.summary: The 2026 FIFA World Cup group stage draw has been completed, setting up several highly anticipated matches. A potential Brazil-Argentina final is among the most intriguing possibilities. Other notable matchups could include a clash between Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo. The full schedule for the tournament has been confirmed, with dates, times, and stadiums announced for all 104 games. ESPN's writers have broken down each group, highlighting key storylines and matchups to watch. The draw has thrown up several exciting clashes, making the 2026 World Cup a highly anticipated event. With top players like Messi, Ronaldo, and others set to take part, the tournament is expected to be unforgettable. The schedule and group stage matchups are now set, paving the way for a thrilling World Cup.

stories.headline: Supreme Court gives in-service teachers time till August 2028 to get TET qualification Supreme Court extends TET qualification deadline for in-service teachers to August 2028, emphasizing children's educational future.
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has extended the deadline for in-service teachers to obtain the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) qualification to August 31, 2028. The original deadline was August 31, 2027. The court's decision aims to prioritize the educational future of children. In-service teachers now have an additional year to pass the TET, which is mandatory for them to remain in service. The extension was granted during hearings on review petitions, with the court emphasizing the importance of the TET qualification for teachers. The new deadline allows teachers more time to prepare and clear the exam, ensuring they can continue to provide education to children without interruption. The court's order upholds the requirement for TET qualification, while providing a more realistic timeline for teachers to comply.

stories.headline: Punjab civic body election results: AAP sweeps over 48% wards, Congress on second spot According to data released by the Punjab State Election Commission, AAP secured victory in 954 out of 1,977 wards
stories.summary: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has secured a significant victory in Punjab's civic body elections, winning 954 out of 1,977 wards. According to the Punjab State Election Commission, this translates to over 48% of the total wards. The Congress party came in second, winning 393 wards, followed by the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) with 192 wards, and the BJP with 172 wards. The results have reinforced Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann's political standing ahead of the next Assembly elections. The AAP's strong performance is seen as a major win for the party, with Chief Minister Mann hailing the results as a significant achievement. The election results reflect the current political landscape in Punjab, with the AAP emerging as a dominant force in the state.

stories.headline: AAP storms into Punjab civic bodies; Congress at second position, SAD trails independents “The people of Punjab have replied to the 'ED party'. 'ED politics' will not work in Punjab,” says Manish Sisodia, as AAP wins more than 45% of the wards.
stories.summary: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has won the Punjab civic body elections, securing 958 wards out of 1,977, accounting for approximately 48% of the total. The Congress party trails behind, while the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) lags behind independents. In various districts, AAP has emerged as the largest party, such as in Ludhiana, where it won 46 seats, and in Jalandhar, where it secured 49 wards. Additionally, 80 candidates were elected unopposed, with AAP leading in this category with 63 uncontested victories. Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann and Deputy Chief Minister Manish Sisodia have hailed the win, stating that the people of Punjab have rejected "politics of hatred" and "ED politics." The election results indicate a strong dominance of AAP in the Punjab civic polls.

stories.headline: Centre clears appointment of 3 judicial officers as additional judges of Karnataka High Court A notification to this effect was issued by the Central government on Friday.
stories.summary: The Central government has cleared the appointment of three judicial officers as additional judges of the Karnataka High Court. A notification was issued on Friday to this effect. The appointments aim to strengthen the bench of the High Court, which is currently functioning with 45 judges, 17 short of its sanctioned strength of 62. The three judicial officers will serve as additional judges for a period of two years from the date they assume charge. The Supreme Court collegium had approved the proposal to elevate the three judicial officers as judges on September 15 and sent the recommendations to the President, leading to the Central government's clearance of their appointments. The move is expected to help reduce the vacancy in the Karnataka High Court.

stories.headline: Trump Set To Finalise Iran Nuclear Deal Tonight
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is set to finalize an Iran nuclear deal tonight, following a memorandum of understanding that is close to completion. The deal aims to prevent Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon and could lead to the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz under a ceasefire framework. Trump has been negotiating with Iran after rejecting a previous proposal, stating that Iran's nuclear program is unacceptable and that they cannot have a nuclear weapon. A temporary ceasefire has been in place since April 8, and Trump has indicated that there is a "very good chance" of reaching an agreement. The President is holding a meeting with his advisors in the White House Situation Room to make a final determination on the deal. The outcome of the meeting is expected to be announced soon.

stories.headline: How are family offices reacting to geopolitical risks?
stories.summary: Family offices are increasing their focus on geopolitical risk management, with 84% considering it the most important issue. According to the 2025 BlackRock Global Family Office Survey, geopolitical uncertainties are forcing family offices to diversify their assets, with 68% reporting a scramble to do so. As a result, allocations to private credit and infrastructure are rising. The 2026 Global Family Office Report from J.P. Morgan Private Bank found that sophisticated investors are leaning into private markets, seeking opportunities in infrastructure, private equity, and growth capital. Despite heightened concerns over geopolitics and trade, family offices are keeping portfolio allocations steady, with some diversifying into cash and liquid alternatives. Geopolitical uncertainty has become the primary concern for family offices globally, significantly influencing capital allocation decisions and overall sentiment.

stories.headline: BREAKING: Trump Set To Finalise Iran Nuclear Deal Tonight? Major Hormuz Strait Breakthrough Near
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is set to finalize a nuclear deal with Iran tonight, with a major breakthrough near on the Strait of Hormuz. A senior Iranian source stated an agreement is close but not yet approved. The deal involves a 60-day ceasefire extension, reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and allowing Iran to freely sell oil. In return, negotiations would be held on curbing Iran's nuclear program. Trump has emphasized that Iran can never possess a nuclear weapon and must end its chokehold on the Strait of Hormuz. The US has also demanded the removal of all enriched uranium from Iran's territory as a condition for a final agreement. Trump is expected to make a "final determination" on the deal tonight, which may include lifting the US naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: US President Donald Trump has signalled that a final decision on a potential Iran agreement could come tonight
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is reviewing a potential agreement with Iran and may make a final decision tonight. The deal, which aims to open the Strait of Hormuz and start nuclear talks, has been awaiting the President's sign-off. Trump had a two-hour meeting on the possible deal but did not make a decision at the time. A tentative ceasefire deal with Iran remains in limbo as the President has yet to announce a final decision. The US and Iran have reached a potential agreement, but Trump's approval is needed to move forward. The President's decision is expected to come soon, with tonight being a possible timeline for the announcement. The agreement's details and implications are still unclear, pending the President's official statement.

stories.headline: Why stock market crashed today? Sensex sinks 1,100 points, Nifty below 23,550. 3 key factors
stories.summary: Indian stock markets plummeted on Friday, with the Sensex sinking 1,100 points and the Nifty falling below 23,550. The decline is attributed to three key factors: persistent foreign investor selling, concerns over a predicted low monsoon, and global market weakness. Rising crude oil prices, which soared above $100/barrel, and the escalating Iran-US tensions also contributed to the downturn. The rupee fell, and bond yields rose, further impacting the market. Additionally, profit booking and persistent outflows by Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) exacerbated the situation. The Stoxx Europe 600 also fell 0.7%, indicating a global market tumble. The Nifty 50 has broken below a rising trendline, indicating a resurgence of bearish sentiment, with potential further correction towards the 23,250 mark and lower levels.

stories.headline: Sensex ends 1,000 points as weak monsoon forecast, Iran uncertainty spook investors
stories.summary: The Sensex plummeted over 1,000 points due to a combination of factors spooking investors. A weak monsoon forecast and uncertainty surrounding the US-Iran deal contributed to the decline. Additionally, MSCI rebalancing and foreign investor selling also played a role in the heavy selling on Thursday. The Nifty slipped below 23,600 as a result. The decline was further exacerbated by rising geopolitical tensions between the US and Iran, as well as a weakening rupee. Investor wealth took a significant hit, with domestic equity benchmarks ending sharply lower. The market volatility was fueled by mixed global cues, leading to a choppy trading session. The weak monsoon forecast and Iran uncertainty have created a perfect storm, leading to a significant decline in the Indian stock market. Investors are navigating the markets with caution amidst the uncertain environment.

stories.headline: Below-normal monsoon forecast, geopolitical jitters trigger 1,092-point Sensex tumble
stories.summary: India's benchmark indices plummeted on May 29, 2026, with the Sensex tumbling 1,092 points to 74,775 and the Nifty falling to 23,547. A below-normal monsoon forecast and geopolitical tensions triggered the sharp decline. The India Meteorological Department predicts rainfall at 92% of the Long Period Average, the lowest initial forecast in 25 years. This, combined with the West Asian conflict, threatens crop production, rural economic growth, and power generation. The last below-normal monsoon occurred in 2023, when the government implemented measures to limit the impact on food inflation. Economists warn that the current situation may pressure growth, inflation, and rural demand, with potential effects on auto sales and the broader economy. The Reserve Bank of India and analysts have expressed concerns about the potential demand shock and disruptions to supply chains.

stories.headline: 6 reasons why Sensex plunged 1,000 points today, Nifty settles below 23,500
stories.summary: The Indian stock market experienced a sharp decline, with the Sensex plunging over 1,000 points and the Nifty slipping below 23,500. This resulted in a ₹9 lakh crore wipeout in market value. The key reasons for the fall include the poor performance of IT stocks, weak global sentiment, and other factors. The decline led to significant losses for investors, with nearly ₹5-6 lakh crore lost in a single session. The IT sector was particularly affected, with Anthropic being a key contributor to the decline. The market's sharp selling pressure resulted in a significant drop in investor wealth, ending the week on a sharply lower note. The Sensex and Nifty's decline marked a significant downturn in the Indian equity market, with investors losing substantial value.

stories.headline: [UCLA Luskin] Samsung’s Bonus Dispute Sparks Calls for Structural Reform Sanford Jacoby weighs in on Samsung Electronics’ performance bonus controversy, recommending a DS division spin-off.
stories.summary: Samsung Electronics' labor-management negotiations over performance bonuses have reached a tentative agreement, averting a total strike. The deal, approved by 74% of voting employees, varies bonuses by tens of millions of won across divisions, with even loss-making divisions receiving large bonuses. Employees in the top-performing chip unit are guaranteed hefty bonuses, while others feel left out, exacerbating pay disparities. The agreement has sparked internal backlash and calls for structural reform, with some recommending a spin-off of the DS division. The controversy highlights concerns over corporate governance, long-term workforce cohesion, and the company's traditional collective growth structure. The deal was brokered through government mediation after a five-month negotiation period, with 62,616 employees participating in the vote.

stories.headline: [CNBC] Software stocks are crashing up. Here are the winners The rally in software stocks has gone from recovery to raging bull market, and traders are betting there's more to come.
stories.summary: The rally in software stocks has transitioned from a recovery phase to a raging bull market, with traders anticipating further growth. Investors are taking bullish positions on software-focused exchange-traded funds (ETFs), indicating confidence in the sector's potential. The technology industry remains optimistic about the long-term prospects of artificial intelligence (AI), despite concerns over valuations. This bullish outlook is driven by growing demand for AI, with industry leaders like Lyft CEO David Risher expressing enthusiasm for its potential. As a result, traders are piling into software stocks, betting on continued gains and a potential return to better market conditions. The sector's performance has been notable, with some areas seeing significant growth over the past few years.

stories.headline: [WBUR] UnitedHealthcare defrauded MassHealth of $100M, AG Campbell alleges United fired back that Campbell's lawsuit is "meritless" and inaccurately captures the purpose of a managed care program.
stories.summary: Massachusetts Attorney General Andrea Campbell has sued UnitedHealthcare Insurance Company, alleging the insurer defrauded MassHealth of at least $100 million. The lawsuit claims UnitedHealthcare misclassified the conditions of elderly members, resulting in inflated payments from the Massachusetts Medicaid program. According to Campbell's office, the insurer's actions likely defrauded MassHealth of at least $100 million due to fraudulent diagnoses. The alleged fraud involves the Senior Care Options (SCO) plan, which requires a health assessment to determine a member's health status. UnitedHealthcare has denied the allegations, calling the lawsuit "meritless" and stating that it inaccurately captures the purpose of the managed care program. The company claims its Senior Care Options program is designed to help seniors with complex care meet their individual health needs. The lawsuit is ongoing, with UnitedHealthcare disputing the allegations.

stories.headline: [Bloomberg.com] Muni Funds Lure Near-Record Cash as Reinvestment Season Nears Investors are pouring money back into municipal bonds as higher yields and the approaching summer reinvestment season draw cash into the tax-exempt market.
stories.summary: Investors are pouring money into municipal bonds due to higher yields and the approaching summer reinvestment season. This influx of cash is drawn to the tax-exempt market, with investors seeking attractive yields and a safe haven from market volatility. Municipal bond funds are experiencing near-record cash inflows, with investors piling in at the fastest rate in five years. The trend is expected to continue, with municipal bonds offering attractive tax-adjusted yields and stable credit quality. Investors in higher tax brackets are particularly drawn to munis as a conservative investment option. As a result, yields have been driven down, but experienced portfolio managers still see value in the market, particularly in longer-term bonds. The summer reinvestment season is expected to further boost the municipal bond market.

stories.headline: AI giant Anthropic reaches near-trillion dollar valuation
stories.summary: Anthropic, an AI giant, has reached a near-trillion dollar valuation, surpassing OpenAI. The company, led by CEO Dario Amodei, announced a $65 billion Series H financing round at a $965 billion valuation. This valuation puts Anthropic ahead of OpenAI, which was valued at $852 billion in March. The latest fundraising round confirms Anthropic's position as a significant player in the AI industry, making it the most valuable artificial intelligence company in Silicon Valley. Anthropic has gained recognition for its coding powers and state-of-the-art technology, solidifying its place in the market. The company's valuation milestone comes as OpenAI is preparing to go public as early as this year. Anthropic's significant valuation underscores its growing influence in the AI sector.

stories.headline: Anthropic Surpasses OpenAI In Valuation After Massive $65 Billion Funding Round
stories.summary: Anthropic has raised $65 billion in a Series H funding round, resulting in a post-money valuation of $965 billion. This surpasses OpenAI's last valuation of $730 billion, making Anthropic the most valuable AI startup. The funding round was led by investors including Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, and Sequoia. Anthropic aims to use the funds to bolster its computing capacity and support the development of its AI technology, including the Claude chatbot. The significant investment reflects the growing competition in the AI sector, with Anthropic and OpenAI emerging as major players. The $965 billion valuation marks a significant milestone for Anthropic, solidifying its position in the industry.

stories.headline: How Anthropic Got So Big, So Fast
stories.summary: Anthropic has secured a $65 billion fund-raising round, catapulting the company to prominence. The AI competitor, maker of Claude, is now nearing a public debut alongside OpenAI, maker of ChatGPT, with a potential $1 trillion valuation. Anthropic's rapid growth has been fueled by its use of its own technology, leading to an infrastructure emergency. To address this, the company has formed an agreement with an unlikely ally. The swift expansion has propelled Anthropic from an also-ran to a leading player in the AI industry, with analysts closely watching its developments. As the company continues to evolve, its growth and strategic partnerships are expected to significantly impact the enterprise landscape. Anthropic's trajectory is being closely monitored, with new developments and updates emerging regularly.

stories.headline: Microsoft-Backed OpenAI Reportedly Grants Japanese Banks Access to Latest AI Model for Cybersecurity
stories.summary: Microsoft-backed OpenAI has granted some Japanese banks access to its latest artificial intelligence model, GPT-5.5. The move aims to enhance the banks' cybersecurity defenses against cyberattacks. Japan's finance minister confirmed the agreement, which will allow top Japanese banks, including MUFG Bank, SMBC, and Mizuho Bank, to utilize the powerful AI tool. The access to GPT-5.5 is expected to bolster the banks' preparedness against cyber threats. The decision comes as financial institutions increasingly rely on AI to strengthen their cybersecurity measures. With this partnership, the Japanese banks will leverage OpenAI's advanced technology to improve their defenses and protect against potential cyberattacks. The collaboration marks a significant step in the adoption of AI in the financial sector for cybersecurity purposes.
